overview: Two of the three major RNA types that cooperate during translation, each with a distinct job in decoding the genetic message.
genZNote: mRNA is the delivery order. tRNA is the delivery driver.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Carries the genetic code copied from DNA to the ribosome, specifying the amino acid sequence of a protein.
aspects.valueB: Adapts the genetic code into amino acids, physically delivering the correct amino acid to the ribosome during translation.

aspects.label: Primary Function
aspects.valueA: Template that is read codon-by-codon during translation.
aspects.valueB: Reads each codon via a complementary anticodon and carries the matching amino acid.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueA: Linear, single-stranded, capped (5') and polyadenylated (3') in eukaryotes.
aspects.valueB: Cloverleaf secondary structure folding into an L-shaped tertiary structure, with an anticodon loop and an amino-acid attachment site.

aspects.label: Relative Abundance and Stability
aspects.valueA: Least abundant RNA type, often short-lived, one mRNA per gene transcript.
aspects.valueB: Stable and abundant, one tRNA species per amino acid/codon family (reused repeatedly).

aspects.label: Biological Context
aspects.valueA: Different mRNA sequence for every protein-coding gene.
aspects.valueB: A relatively small, conserved set of tRNAs (~20 major types matching the amino acids) shared across proteins.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Decodes the message and delivers amino acids (anticodons).
